Chapter 7: Embracing Risk and Learning from Failure
If you really want to build wealth, there’s no way around it — you’ve got to be willing to step into the unknown. Whether you’re thinking about starting a business, investing, or maybe chasing after a new career, risk is always going to be along for the ride.
But have you ever wondered why some people seem to thrive in these situations, while others stay stuck, playing it safe? Most of the time, it comes down to how you see risk and how you handle failure.
A lot of us grew up learning to steer clear of risk, thinking it’s dangerous or even embarrassing. But here’s the truth: any real change—anything that actually matters—brings some uncertainty with it. The trick isn’t to avoid risk entirely, but to approach it with a clear head, instead of letting fear take the wheel.
So, what does embracing risk really look like in your day-to-day life? Here’s a practical way to think about it:
First, try to look at possible downsides honestly, without blowing them out of proportion.
Next, take small, manageable steps—not wild leaps that leave you with nowhere to land.
And when things don’t go as planned, treat each setback as feedback—not as some kind of judgment on who you are.
Over time, you can actually build up what I like to call your “failure resilience” muscle. How? By taking a step back after things go sideways, asking yourself what happened, and thinking about what you could do differently next time.
Imagine someone launching a side business. Instead of risking everything on instant success, they might start with a small pilot project. Maybe it doesn’t go perfectly at first, but each early mistake is just another lesson. They adjust, they keep learning, and gradually, they grow.
It’s a lot like learning to ride a bike, isn’t it? You expect to fall a few times. But with every try, you get a little steadier, a little more confident. After a while, the fear of falling fades, and you start to focus on what’s possible.
When you start to see risk as normal—and failure as just part of the process—suddenly, those big opportunities don’t seem so far out of reach. That shift in mindset? It’s not just helpful. It’s absolutely essential if you want to build real, lasting wealth.
